tier_reason: README shows first-party fillarray output: scalar xorshift128+ 3.63 cycles/value vs AVX-512 two-stream 1.47 (AVX2 2.21, AVX2 two-stream 1.88) on 'a Skylake-X processor'. Benchmark code (benchmark/fillarray.c) and Makefile flags are public, but the compiler is unnamed (plain $(CC)) and no exact CPU model is given, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Skylake-X, 5000 32-bit values: scalar xorshift128+ 3.63 cycles/value; AVX2 2.21; AVX2 two-stream 1.88; AVX-512 two-stream 1.47 (~2.5x, derived from page data)
corrections.baseline: scalar xorshift128+ (Vigna's reference C implementation, same algorithm)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 125 stars, 17 forks; README says used by ClickHouse
corrections.caveats: Baseline is the scalar version of the same generator, not mt19937/PCG; compiler unnamed and CPU given only as 'Skylake-X'; xorshift128+ fails BigCrush (README); README notes gains shrink in shuffling where other bottlenecks dominate; requires Haswell+ (AVX2) or AVX-512

notes: Numbers match README exactly. Last commit 2020-07-22 (>3 years), so abandoned; Apache-2.0 confirmed via LICENSE file.

tier_reason: README has no performance numbers; benchmark/ holds only a bench_normal_distribution target (Makefile, -O2 -mtune=native -funsafe-math-optimizations) with no published results.
notes: Real BSL-1.0 header-only drop-in for std::normal_distribution, but tier D with 4 stars is not notable. License file is LICENSE.txt (Boost).

tier_reason: Upgraded from D: the full paper (arXiv v7) times one billion 32-bit numbers on an Intel Core i7-9700 with gcc 11.2.0 (Cygwin64): Philox 4x32-10 2.29 s vs Squares 1.35 s. These are the author's own numbers, the paper is not peer-reviewed, and flags and the Philox implementation are unstated, so the tier is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 1e9 32-bit randoms: Philox 4x32-10 2.29 s vs squares32 1.35 s (~1.7x, derived from page data); 64-bit squares split into two 32-bit halves 1.23 s; 53-bit float output 1.93 s
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 11.2.0 under Cygwin64; optimization flags not stated
corrections.caveats: First-party, non-peer-reviewed arXiv paper; optimization flags and Philox implementation source not stated; code is distributed from the author's website (squaresrng.wixsite.com/rand), license not checked; no comparison against Threefry/mt19937 timings found

notes: The Philox numbers appear only in the PDF body, not on the abstract page. Code site not opened, so the license is unknown and usability stays reference; has_code may be true (software package offered) but the site is unverified.
